• and His saying: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need, and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6],

• and His saying: ﴿They say, "Allah has taken a son." Glory be to Him; He is the Free of need﴾ [Yunus: 68],

along with other verses.

So Allah, blessed and exalted, commands the creation and forbids them, not because their disobedience harms Him or their obedience benefits Him, but rather the benefit of their obedience is for them and the harm of their disobedience is upon them, as He, exalted, said: ﴿If you do good, you do good for your own souls; and if you do evil, then it is for them﴾ [al-Isra': 7], and He said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾ [Fussilat: 46], and He said: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15].

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in what he narrates from his Lord, that He said: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not add anything to My dominion. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not diminish anything from My dominion," the hadith.

Note:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾, after His saying: ﴿And due to Allah from the people is pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], indicates that whoever does not perform Hajj is a disbeliever, and Allah is free of need from him.

Regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾, the scholars have several views. The first: the meaning of His saying ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾ is, i.e., whoever denies the obligation of Hajj, then he has disbelieved, and Allah is free of need from him. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and others, as reported by Ibn Kathir. This view is supported by what is narrated from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid that they said: when the verse was revealed, ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85], the Jews said: "We are Muslims."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has enjoined upon the Muslims the Hajj to the House for whoever is able to find thereto a way." They said: "It has not been prescribed for us," and they refused to perform Hajj. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97].

The second view: the meaning of His saying ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97] is, i.e., whoever does not perform Hajj, as a severe expression of warning against abandoning Hajj while having the ability, like His saying to al-Miqdad, established in the two Sahihs, when he asked him about killing a disbeliever who had embraced Islam after his hand had been cut off in battle: "Do not kill him; for if you kill him, he is in your position before you kill him, and you are in his position before he spoke the word he spoke."

The third view: to take the verse according to its apparent meaning, and that whoever does not perform Hajj while having the ability has disbelieved.

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever possesses provision and a mount, and does not perform Hajj to the House of Allah, it does not harm him whether he dies a Jew or a Christian; and that is because Allah said: ﴿And due to Allah from the people is pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. And whoever disbelieves - indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾" [Al 'Imran: 97].

This hadith was related by at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh, as Ibn Kathir reported from them, and it is a weak hadith, declared weak by more than one scholar because its chain contains Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah, mawla of Rabi'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili, and this Hilal. at-Tirmidhi said: "Unknown (majhul)." al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith." And its chain also contains al-Harith, who narrated it from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him). at-Tirmidhi said: "He is weak in hadith." Ibn 'Adi said: "This hadith is not preserved." Concluded in substance from Ibn Kathir.

Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi ash-Shaf fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf: At-Tirmidhi transmitted this hadith from the narration of Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bahili: Abu Ishaq narrated to us from al-Harith, from 'Ali, raising it: "Whoever possesses provision and a mount that conveys him to the House of Allah, and does not perform Hajj, there is no blame upon him if he dies a Jew or a Christian."

He said: It is gharib, and its chain has problems; Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah is unknown, and al-Harith is weak. al-Bazzar transmitted it through this route and said: we do not know it from 'Ali except through this route. Ibn 'Adi and al-Uqayli transmitted it in the biography of Hilal, and it is reported from al-Bukhari that he is munkar al-hadith.

al-Bayhaqi said in ash-Shu'ab: Hilal alone transmitted it, and it has a witness from the hadith of Abu Umamah, transmitted by ad-Darimi with the wording: "Whoever is not prevented from Hajj by an apparent need, or an oppressive ruler, or a restraining illness, and dies, let him die, if he wishes, a Jew, or if he wishes, a Christian." It was transmitted through the narration of Sharik from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from him. By this route al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it in ash-Shu'ab. Ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted it from Abu al-Ahwas, from Layth, from 'Abd al-Rahman, as a mursal, without mentioning Abu Umamah. Ibn al-Jawzi included it in al-Mawdu'at through the route of Ibn 'Adi; and Ibn 'Adi included it in al-Kamil in the biography of Abu al-Mahzum Yazid ibn Sufyan, from Abu Hurayrah, raised, similar to it. He related from al-Qallas that he declared Abu al-Mahzum a liar. This is an error of Ibn al-Jawzi in his handling, because the route to Abu Umamah does not contain anyone accused of lying.

It has been authentically reported from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: whoever was able to perform Hajj but did not perform it, then whether he dies a Jew or a Christian is the same. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 102:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ — the verse. Most scholars hold that it has been abrogated (mansukh) by His saying: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun: 16].

Some said: it clarifies what is meant by it, so His saying ﴿as He should be feared﴾ means: according to capacity, and Allah knows best.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ — the verse.

This verse indicates an extreme emphasis on fearing Allah, exalted is He, and another verse has come that indicates otherwise, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun: 16]. The answer is in two matters:

The first: the verse ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ abrogates His saying ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾. This view was held by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Suddi and others, as related by Ibn Kathir.

The second: it clarifies the intended meaning of it, and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 103:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you, when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so that by His favour you became brothers﴾. He did not specify here the degree of hostility they had reached, but He explained in another place that their hostility reached a great severity, to the extent that even if one spent all that is on earth to remove it and to join their hearts together, it would not avail anything. That is in His words: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah. It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers. And He brought their hearts together. Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but Allah brought them together. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [al-Anfal: 62–63].

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Illusion of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And you were on the brink of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it﴾.

This noble verse indicates that the Ansar had between them and the Fire nothing but death, although they (p-242) were people of a fatra (a gap between prophets). Yet Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15].

And He says: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [an-Nisa: 165]. Allah, exalted is He, has explained this argument in His words in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we are humiliated and disgraced"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134]. Verses similar to this are many.

What appears correct in the answer, and Allah knows best, is that with the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) no excuse remains for anyone. So everyone who does not believe in him has between himself and the Fire nothing but death.

This is as Allah has explained by His words: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17]. As for what some of them answered, that they retained a remnant of the warning of earlier messengers by which the argument binds them, that is a false answer, because the texts of the Qur'an explicitly state that no warner had come to them, as in His words: ﴿That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6].

And His words: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾ [as-Sajdah: 3].

And His words: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We called, but it was a mercy from your Lord that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾ [al-Qasas: 46].

And His words: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you after a gap in the messengers, lest you say, "There came to us no bringer of good news and no warner"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 19].

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We had not given them any books they could study, nor had We sent to them before you any warner﴾ [Saba: 44].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And faces will be blackened﴾. In this noble verse He made clear that one of the causes of faces being blackened on the Day of Resurrection is disbelief after faith, as in His saying: ﴿As for those whose faces are blackened: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 106], and so on.

In another place He made clear that one of the causes of this is lying against Allah, exalted is He, as in His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied against Allah with their faces blackened﴾ [al-Zumar: 60]. In another place He made clear that one of the causes of this is earning evil deeds, as in His saying: ﴿And those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is its like, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night﴾ [Yunus: 27]. In another place He made clear that one of the causes of this is disbelief and wickedness, as in His saying: (p-206) ﴿And faces that Day will have dust upon them, darkness will cover them. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 40–42].

In reality these causes are one thing, expressed in different phrases, namely disbelief in Allah, exalted is He. In another place He made clear the severity of the disfigurement of their faces by blueness of the eyes, as in His saying: ﴿And We will gather the criminals on that Day, blue-eyed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102]. The most hideous image is for the faces to be black and the eyes to be blue. Do you not see that the poet, when he wished to depict the faults of the miser in the most hideous and ugly form, devised for them blueness of the eyes and blackness of the faces, in his saying:

"For the miser, over his wealth, are excuses, blue-eyed, upon them are faces that are black."

He said, "Among the People of the Book is a community standing [in obedience], reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night while they prostrate." Here he mentions among the attributes of this believing group from the People of the Book that they are "standing," that is, upright and steadfast upon the truth, that they recite the verses of God during the night hours, that they pray, that they believe in God, that they enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil.

He mentions elsewhere that they recite the Book with its due recitation and believe in God, as in His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it should be recited; they believe in it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 121].

He mentions elsewhere that they believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to them, and that they are humble before God and do not trade away His verses for a small price, as in His saying: ﴿And among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to God, not exchanging the verses of God for a small price﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 199]. He mentions elsewhere that they rejoice at the revelation of the Qur'an, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those to whom We gave the Book rejoice at what has been revealed to you﴾ [al-Ra'd: 36]. He mentions elsewhere that they know that the revelation of the Qur'an is from God and is true, as in His saying: ﴿And those to whom We gave the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾ (the verse) [al-An'am: 114]. He mentions elsewhere that when the Qur'an is recited to them, they fall down on their faces in prostration, glorify their Lord, and weep, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their faces in prostration﴾ ﴿and say, "Glory be to our Lord; the promise of our Lord has indeed been fulfilled"﴾ ﴿And they fall down on their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility﴾ [al-Isra': 107–109].

He also spoke of their weeping upon hearing it, in His saying: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83]. (p-207) He mentions elsewhere that this group from the People of the Book will be given their reward twice, as in His saying: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, that they might be reminded﴾ ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it—they believe in it﴾ ﴿And when it is recited to them, they say, "We have believed in it; indeed it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it."﴾ ﴿Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured﴾ [al-Qasas: 51–54].

His saying, exalted is He: "and you believe in the Book, all of it" (wa-tu'minuna bil-kitabi kullihi), i.e., you believe in all the books, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: "Say, I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down" (Ash-Shura 42:15), and His saying: "Each one believes in Allah and His angels and His books" (Al-Baqarah 2:285).

The author said in *Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab* (*Repelling the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book*):

Allah Most High said: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak﴾.

In this verse Allah describes the believers as weak (*adhillah*) at the time He gave them victory at Badr. In another verse He describes them as possessing honour (*ʿizzah*), where He says: ﴿And honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8]. The contrast and opposition between honour and weakness are evident.

The answer is clear. The meaning of describing them as weak is the fewness of their number and their equipment on the day of Badr. (p-243) His statement: ﴿And honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ was revealed during the campaign of al-Muraysiʿ (*ghazwah*, a military expedition), which is the campaign of Banu al-Mustaliq, after the power of the Muslims had grown strong and their number and equipment had increased. Honour and weakness can also be reconciled by another consideration: weakness is considered in terms of the condition of the Muslims, in their fewness of number and equipment, while honour is considered in terms of Allah's help and support. This is indicated by His statement: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people would snatch you away, so He gave you refuge and strengthened you with His help﴾ [al-Anfal: 26].

As for His statement: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak﴾ [Al ʿImran: 123], the time of the state (*zaman al-hal*) is the same as the time of its governing verb (*ʿamil*). Thus the time of the victory is the time of their being weak. It is therefore clear that the description of weakness is in one respect, and the description of victory and honour is in another respect. The aspects are separate. And Allah knows best.

The author said, in (Raf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾

This verse indicates that the reinforcement of angels on the Day of Badr was from three thousand up to five thousand. And He, exalted is He, mentioned in the surah of "al-Anfal" that this reinforcement was one thousand, in His saying: ﴿When you were seeking help from your Lord, and He answered you, "I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another."﴾ [al-Anfal: 9].

The answer to this is in two respects:

The first: He promised them one thousand at first, then it became three thousand, then it became five thousand, as in this verse.

The second respect: the verse of "al-Anfal" did not limit itself to the thousand, but rather alluded to the increase mentioned in "Al 'Imran," especially in the recitation of Nafi': "with a thousand angels, following [mardifin]" [al-Anfal: 9], with the letter dal vocalized with a fatha in the passive form (murdafin), because the meaning of "mardifin" is "those who are followed by others," and this is the truth.

As for those who say that the reinforcement mentioned in "Al 'Imran" was on the Day of Uhud, and the one mentioned in "al-Anfal" was on the Day of Badr (p-344), there is no difficulty for their view, except that no reinforcement of angels came in the battle of Uhud.

The answer: the coming of the reinforcement in it, according to this view, was conditional upon patience and piety, in His saying: ﴿Yes, if you are patient and mindful of Allah, and they come upon you suddenly from this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked [for battle].﴾ [Al 'Imran: 125], and since they were not patient and did not fear Allah, the reinforcement did not come. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Zuhri, Musa ibn 'Uqbah and others; so said Ibn Kathir.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 133:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth﴾. He means: its breadth is like the breadth of the heavens and the earth, as His saying, exalted is He, in Surat al-Hadid clarifies: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose breadth is like the breadth of the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 21]. The verse of "Al 'Imran" here shows that what is meant by "the heaven" in the verse of "al-Hadid" is its genus, which encompasses all the heavens, as is apparent, and Allah knows best.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾. The wound that touched the Muslims is what befell them on the Day of Uhud of killing and injury, as the Exalted indicated in this noble surah in several places, such as His saying: ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it. Now you have seen it, while you were looking on﴾ [Al 'Imran: 143], His saying: ﴿and that He might take martyrs from among you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140 etc.], His saying: ﴿until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He showed you that which you love, among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152], His saying: ﴿when you were ascending and not turning back to anyone while the Messenger was calling you from your rear﴾ [Al 'Imran: 153], and similar verses.

As for the wound that touched the disbelieving people, it is possible that it is what befell them on the Day of Badr of killing and capture. In that case, the reference is His saying: ﴿When your Lord inspired to the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip." That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty﴾ [Al-Anfal: 12-13].

It is also possible that it refers to the initial defeat of the polytheists on the Day of Uhud, as will come shortly, God willing. He has indicated both wounds together with His saying: ﴿Why, when a disaster struck you although you had struck [the enemy] with twice as much, do you say, "From where is this?"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 165]. So the disaster of the Muslims is the wound that touched them on the Day of Uhud, and the disaster of the disbelievers, [which was] twice that, is the wound that touched them before, on the Day of Badr; because on the Day of Uhud seventy of the Muslims were killed, and on the Day of Badr seventy of the disbelievers were killed and seventy were taken captive.

This is the view of the majority. Some scholars have mentioned that the disaster that befell the polytheists was what befell them on the Day of Uhud of killing and defeat, when the standard-bearers from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar were killed, and the polytheists were routed at the beginning of the affair with a shameful rout, and their standard remained fallen until 'Amrah bint 'Alqamah al-Harithiyyah raised it. Concerning that, Hassan said, [from al-Tawil]:

"Had it not been for the standard of al-Harithiyyah, they would have been sold in the markets, sold like captives."

In this view, the wound that struck the disbelieving people is referred to by the Exalted's saying: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152]. The meaning of "tahussunahum" is: you kill them and eradicate them. Its root is from "hiss" (sense perception through the senses), so the meaning of "hassahu" is that he removed its sense by killing. From this is Jarir's saying [from al-Wafir]:

"The swords strip them as the fire of a blaze spreads in a thicket of harvested reeds."

And another's saying [from al-Tawil]:

"We stripped them of sense with the sword, a stripping, so their remnants became scattered and dispersed."

And Ru'bah's saying [from al-Rajaz]:

"When we complain of a year of drought that devours what remains after the green has become dry."

He means by "the devastating year" the barren year that consumes everything. We have previously mentioned in the introduction to this book that the verse may have two possibilities, and each of them is supported by [another] Qur'an, and both are true, so we mention both together and what supports each of them.

Some scholars have said: The context indicates that the wound that touched the polytheists is what befell them on the Day of Uhud, because the discourse is about the battle of Uhud. However, the dual form in His saying "mithlayha" (twice that) indicates that the wound that touched the polytheists is what befell them on the Day of Badr, because no one has reported that the disbelievers on the Day of Uhud were struck with twice what the Muslims were struck with. There is no proof in His saying "tahussunahum," because that stripping and eradication was specifically of those among the polytheists who were killed, and they were fewer than those of the Muslims who were killed on the Day of Uhud, as is well known.

If it is said: What is the reconciliation between the singular in His saying "wound similar to it" [Al 'Imran: 140] and the dual in His saying "you had struck [them] with twice as much"? The answer, and Allah knows best, is that the dual refers to the killing of seventy and the capture of seventy on the Day of Badr, in return for seventy on the Day of Uhud, as the majority of scholars hold.

The singular "similar" is meant to liken wound to wound in general sense of harm and pain. The two canonical recitations (qira'at) of His saying: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people﴾ [Al 'Imran: 140], with the letter qaf vocalized with fatha or with damma in both occurrences, have the same meaning; they are two dialects, like "al-da'f" and "al-du'f" (weakness).

Al-Farra' said: "Qarh" with fatha is the wound, and with damma is its pain. End. Among the Arabs' usage of "qarh" for a wound is the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah al-Tamimi [from al-Tawil]:

"Sit, do not let me hear reproach from you, and do not reopen the wound of the heart so that it aches."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 142:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive and made evident those who are steadfast?﴾ In this verse, Allah denounces those who think they will enter Paradise without being tested with the severe obligations by which the distinction is made between the steadfast one who is sincere in his religion and others. He clarified this meaning in several verses, such as His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed on before you? They were touched by misfortune and adversity and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 214]. And His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone while Allah has not yet made evident those among you who strive and did not take other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers as intimate friends? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 16]. And His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do the people think they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested? And We had already tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 1-3].

In these verses there is a subtle secret, a lesson and a wisdom. That is because our father Adam was in Paradise, eating from it freely wherever he wished, in the most complete blessing, the fullest happiness and the most pleasant life, as his Lord said to him: ﴿Indeed, it is [granted] to you that you will not be hungry therein or be unclothed. And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein or be exposed to the sun.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 118-119]. Had we multiplied (p-210) therein, we would have been in the most pleasant life and the most complete blessing. But Iblis, upon whom be the curses of Allah, deceived our two parents by his cunning and deception until he removed them from Paradise to the abode of wretchedness and toil.

At that point Allah, may He be exalted, decreed that none would enter His Paradise except after being tested with hardships and the difficulty of obligations. So it is incumbent upon the intelligent among us, O assembly of the children of Adam, to picture the reality and know that we are in truth captives whom Iblis has taken by his cunning and deception from our noble homeland to the abode of wretchedness and affliction. Therefore, one should strive against his enemy Iblis and his soul that commands to evil until he returns to the noble first homeland, as Ibn al-Qayyim said [al-Tawil]:

"But we are captives of the enemy, so will we be seen returned to our homelands and safe?"

For this wisdom, Allah, may He be exalted, repeated in His Book the mention of the story of Iblis with Adam, so that it might be before our eyes constantly.

He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, with whom were many devoted servants (ribbiyyun)...﴾ [the verse]. This noble verse, according to the reading of the one who reads "qutila" (was killed) in the passive voice, may have its deputy subject (na'ib al-fa'il) be the word "ribbiyyun." In that case there is no pronoun in "qutila" at all. It is also possible that the deputy subject is a pronoun referring back to the Prophet. In that case "ma'ahu" (with him) is a predicate placed first, and "ribbiyyun" is a postponed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar). What justifies beginning with an indefinite noun here is that it depends on the adverbial phrase before it and is described by what follows it. The clause is a circumstantial clause (hal), and its linking element is the pronoun. What makes it permissible for a circumstantial clause to come from the indefinite noun "nabiyy" is describing it with being killed unjustly. This is the best of the grammatical analyses (i'rab, the grammatical parsing of words) mentioned for this verse according to this view. With these two possibilities regarding the deputy subject, it becomes clear that the verse is ambiguous (ijmal).

The Qur'anic verses make clear that the prophet who fights is not defeated but is victorious, as God stated explicitly in His saying: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail."﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21]. Before this He said: ﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾ [al-Mujadila: 20], and after it He said: ﴿Indeed, God is Strong and Mighty﴾.

Most of the meanings of "ghalaba" (overcoming, prevailing) in the Qur'an refer to overcoming by the sword and the spear, such as His saying:
• ﴿If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are a hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾ [al-Anfal: 65];
• and His saying: ﴿So if there are among you a hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand﴾;
• and His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been overcome, in the nearest land; but after their defeat they will overcome, within a few years﴾ [al-Rum: 1–4];
• and His saying: ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company﴾ [al-Baqarah: 249];
• and His saying: Say to ﴿those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 12];
and other verses besides these.

(p. 211) He, may He be exalted, also made clear that the one who is killed is not a victor, but rather a category opposed to the victor, by His saying: ﴿And whoever fights in the cause of God and is killed or overcomes, We will bestow upon him a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 74]. It becomes evident from these verses that killing does not befall the prophet who fights, because God has decreed and determined for him from eternity that he is a victor, and He explicitly stated that the one who is killed is not a victor.

Scholars have established that the prophets' overcoming is of two kinds: overcoming by proof and clear explanation, which belongs to all of them, and overcoming by the sword and the spear, which belongs specifically to those among them who were commanded to fight in the cause of God. This is because whoever was not commanded to fight is neither a victor nor a vanquished, since he did not contend in anything. God's explicit statement that He decreed that His messengers would be victorious includes their overcoming of whoever opposed them by the sword, as we have shown that this is the meaning of "ghalaba" in the Qur'an, and it also includes their overcoming by proof and clear explanation. Thus it clarifies that the help of the messengers mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and in His saying: ﴿And已 Our word has already preceded for Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victors﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–172], is help of overcoming by the sword and the spear for those among them who were commanded to strive. This is because the overcoming that He stated He had decreed for them is more specific than general help, since it is a particular help. Linguistically, "ghalaba" means subjugation, and "nasr" (help) linguistically means aiding the oppressed. Therefore the general meaning must be explained by the more specific one.

By this you know that what the great imam Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) and those who followed him said, in interpreting His saying ﴿Indeed, We will surely help﴾, is mistaken. They said there is no barrier to the killing of a messenger who was commanded to strive, and that the help stated in the verse must be understood in one of two ways:

The first: that God helps him after death, by empowering over those who killed him someone who will avenge him, as He did with those who killed Yahya, Zakariyya and Sha'ya, by empowering Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtunassar) over them, and similar things.

The second: that the messengers in His saying "Indeed, We will surely help Our messengers" refers specifically to our Prophet (ﷺ) alone. But it is not permissible to interpret the Qur'an this way, for two reasons:

The first: it is a departure from the apparent and immediate meaning of the Book of God without evidence from the Qur'an, the Sunnah or consensus (ijma'). The ruling that the one killed among those fighting is the one who is helped is very far-fetched and not known in the language of the Arabs. So interpreting the Qur'an that way without evidence is a manifest error. Similarly, restricting the messengers to our Prophet (ﷺ) alone is also very far-fetched. The verses indicating the general promise of help for all the messengers are numerous, and there is no dispute about them.

(p. 212) The second: God did not limit His Book to general help, which in language means aiding the oppressed. Rather, He explicitly stated that this mentioned help for the messengers is help of overcoming, by His saying: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21]. You have seen the meaning of "ghalaba" in the Qur'an, and it has passed before you that God made the one killed a category opposed to the victor in His saying: ﴿And whoever fights in the cause of God and is killed or overcomes﴾. He also stated explicitly that what He promised His messengers cannot be changed, by His saying, may He be majestic and exalted: ﴿And messengers before you were denied, but they endured patiently what they were denied and what they suffered, until Our help came to them. None can alter the words of God. And there has already come to you some information about the messengers﴾ [al-An'am: 34]. There is no doubt that His saying, ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], is among His words, of which He explicitly stated that none can change them. And He, may He be majestic and exalted, categorically negated for the one who is helped that he could be defeated, by His saying: ﴿If God helps you, none can overcome you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 160]. Muqatil mentioned that the occasion of revelation of His saying, ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21], was that some people said: "Does Muhammad and his companions think they will overcome the Romans and the Persians, as they overcame the Arabs?" claiming that the Romans and Persians could not be overcome by the Prophet (ﷺ) because of their number and strength. So God revealed the verse. This indicates that the overcoming mentioned in it is overcoming by the sword and the spear, because the occasion of revelation cannot be excluded from the ruling. It is supported by His saying before it: ﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾ [al-Mujadila: 20], and His saying after it: ﴿Indeed, God is Strong and Mighty﴾.

We have already stated in the introduction to this book that we cite, in support of the clarification, a non-canonical reading (shadhdhah) alongside the canonical seven readings (qira'at sab'iyyah). The clarification we have given is supported by the fact that the deputy subject is "ribbiyyun," and that some readers other than the Seven read "qutthila ma'ahu ribbiyyun" with the doubled letter (tashdid), because the multiplication indicated by the doubling requires that the killing befell the ribbiyyun.

Al-Zamakhshari, al-Baydawi and Ibn Jinni preferred, on the basis of this reading, that the deputy subject is "ribbiyyun." Al-Alusi also inclined to this in his tafsir, clarifying that the claim that the doubling does not contradict the killing befalling the Prophet is because "ka'ayyin" is an indication of a large number, meaning: many individuals of the prophets were killed. This is contrary to the apparent meaning, and it is as he said.

If it is objected: We have learned that the deputy subject mentioned is capable of two possibilities, and you have claimed that the Qur'an indicates that it is "ribbiyyun" and not the pronoun of the Prophet, because it explicitly says the messengers are victors, and the one who is killed is not a victor. We say that the Qur'an, in other verses, indicates that the deputy subject is the pronoun of the Prophet, because it explicitly states in many verses that some messengers were killed, such as His saying: ﴿So some you denied, and some you kill﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87], and His saying: ﴿Say: "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you have said. Then why did you kill them?"﴾ (p. 213) [Al 'Imran: 183]. So what is the basis for preferring what you have used as evidence that the deputy subject is "ribbiyyun" over what we have used as evidence that the deputy subject is the pronoun of the Prophet?

The answer has three aspects:

The first: What we used as evidence is more specific than what you used as evidence, and the more specific takes precedence over the more general. A general and a specific text do not conflict, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh, the foundations of Islamic legal theory). Its clarification is that our evidence concerns a particular prophet who was commanded to contend in something, so we are certain that he prevailed in it, in confirmation of our Lord's saying: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾, whether that contention was by proof and clear explanation or by the sword and the spear. Your evidence concerns what is more general than this, because the verses that indicated the killing of some messengers did not indicate that it occurred in a specific jihad. Rather, their apparent meaning is that it was outside of jihad, as will be made clear.

The second aspect: all the verses indicating that some messengers were killed by the enemies of God are, in every instance, about the Children of Israel killing their prophets, outside of jihad and fighting, except for the single point of dispute.

The third aspect: what we have preferred, that the deputy subject is "ribbiyyun," agrees with the verses of the Qur'an in clear agreement with no ambiguity, according to the requirements of the Arabic language in its most eloquent forms. Two verses have not conflicted with each other from it, since we have understood the killed messenger to be one who was not commanded to strive. So his killing is then without any problem, and it does not lead to opposing any single verse of the Book of God. This is because God ruled that the messengers would be victorious, and victory is only with contention, and this one was not commanded to contend in anything. Had he been commanded to contend in something, he would have prevailed in it. But if we say the deputy subject is the pronoun of the Prophet, the meaning becomes that many of the prophets who fought were killed on the battlefield, as the emphatic form "ka'ayyin" followed by "min nabiyy" indicates. The killing of this great number of fighting prophets on the battlefield by the enemies is in explicit contradiction to His saying: "God has decreed: 'I and My messengers will surely prevail.'" You have come to know the meaning of overcoming in the Qur'an, and you have come to know that He, may He be exalted, made clear that the one killed is not the victor, as has been stated before. This Mighty Book was not revealed so that some of it strikes others, but it was revealed so that some of it confirms others. Thus it became clear that the Qur'an indicates clearly that the deputy subject is "ribbiyyun," and that no messenger was killed in jihad, as al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Zajjaj, al-Farra' and others besides them have affirmed. In this book we intended to clarify by the Qur'an, not by the sayings of scholars, and for this reason we have not quoted the views of those who preferred what we have mentioned.

As for what some scholars used to prefer that the deputy subject is the pronoun of the Prophet, namely that the occasion of revelation indicates this, because the occasion of its revelation was that the one who cried out shouted "Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed," and that His saying ﴿Then if he dies or is killed﴾ (p. 214) [Al 'Imran: 144] indicates this, and that His saying ﴿So they did not weaken for what befell them in the cause of God﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146] indicates that the "ribbiyyun" were not killed, because if they had been killed He would not have said about them: "So they did not weaken for what befell them" — this is all baseless speech and preferences on which nothing can be relied. As for preference by the occasion of revelation, it is that if the occasion of revelation required specifying the mention of the Prophet's killing, then the majority's reading "qatala" (fought) in the past tense of the form of mutual engagement would be running contrary to what is required, and this is clearly untenable as you see. As for the preference by His saying "Then if he dies or is killed," it is clearly untenable, because both are conditioned by the conditional particle, and what is conditioned by it does not indicate that an attribution has occurred at all, neither affirmatively nor negatively, so that something else could be preferred by it.

And when we look at the actual reality (al-waqi' fi nafs al-amr), we find that their Prophet ﷺ was not killed at that time, nor did he die. The preponderance (al-tarjih) by His saying, ﴿So they did not weaken﴾, that it had fallen is as clear as the sun at mid-morning. And the greatest decisive proof of its fall is the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i: ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein. But if they fight you, then kill them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 191], where all the verbs are from killing (al-qatl), not from fighting (al-qital). This reading is among the seven widely transmitted (mutawatir) readings. For qataluukum without an alif after the qaf is a past-tense verb from killing (al-qatl), and then "fa-qtuluhum" (so kill them). Would you say this is not valid? Because the one who has been killed cannot be commanded to kill his killer.

Rather, the meaning is "qatalu ba'dakum" (some of you were killed), and this is a well-known meaning in the Arabic language. They say: "qataluna" (they killed us) and "qatalnahum" (we killed them), meaning the occurrence of killing upon some, as is not hidden. We have already pointed to this clarification in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Illusion of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 153:

The author said in (Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab, "Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book"):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what befell you﴾, and so on.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So He rewarded you with grief upon grief﴾ means: grief upon grief, that is, sorrow upon sorrow. Or it means: He rewarded you with grief because of your grief for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), due to disobedience to his command. According to what first comes to mind, the expression that fits this grief would be "in order that you would grieve." As for His saying, "so that you would not grieve," it is problematic, because grief is a cause of sorrow, not of its absence.

The answer to this is given in several respects:

The first: His saying, ﴿so that you would not grieve﴾ is connected to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah had already pardoned you﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 152]. Accordingly, the meaning is that He, exalted is He, pardoned you so that the sweetness of His pardon would remove from you what you had suffered of the grief of killing and wounds, the loss of the spoils and victory, and the distress from the rumour that the Prophet (ﷺ) had been killed by the polytheists.

The second respect: the meaning of the verse is that He, exalted is He, caused you this grief so that you would become accustomed to the calamities of time, so that sorrow would not reach you in the future, because whoever is accustomed to misfortunes, they do not affect him.

The third respect: that "lā" is a connecting particle (wasla). The discussion of its being an added particle, with its Arabic evidences, will come, God willing, in the reconciliation between His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I swear by this city﴾ [90:1], and His saying: ﴿and this secure city﴾ [95:3].

The Qur'anic verse (3:156): ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled through the land or were raiders, "If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed."﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 156:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled through the land or were raiders, "If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed."﴾ In this noble verse, He mentions that when some of the hypocrites' brothers die, they say: "If they had obeyed us and not gone out to the raid, they would not have been killed." It does not state here whether they say this to them before the journey to the raid in order to discourage them (yuthabbitu, to dishearten or deter) or not. A parallel to this verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who said to their brothers while they sat back, "If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 168]. But in other verses He explains that they say this to them before the raid in order to discourage them, as in His saying: "And they said, Do not go forth in the heat" (the verse) [al-Tawbah: 81], and His saying: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who hinder others and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18], and His saying: ﴿And indeed among you is one who lingers﴾ [4], and other verses besides these.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 157:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or you die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate﴾. In this noble verse, He mentioned that the one who is killed in jihad (struggle in the way of Allah) and the one who dies both attain (p-215) forgiveness from Allah and mercy, which is better for him than the perishable goods of this world that he gathers. The clearest explanation of this is in another verse, in which He stated that Allah has purchased from them a short, perishable life, troubled by calamities and pains, in exchange for an everlasting, delightful life that never ends and in which its owner is never harmed by anything; and He purchased from them a little, perishable wealth in exchange for a dominion that never runs out and never ends. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a true promise upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an. And who is truer in His promise than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment﴾ [At-Tawbah: 111]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾ [Al-Insan: 20]. In another verse, He made clear that the bounty of Allah and His mercy are better than what the people of this world accumulate of its goods, and He added to it the command to rejoice in the bounty of Allah and His mercy rather than in the goods of this world. This is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, let them rejoice; that is better than what they accumulate"﴾ [Yunus: 58]. The fronting of the object (taqdim al-ma'mul) indicates restriction (al-hasr), I mean His saying: ﴿in that let them rejoice﴾, that is, rather than anything else, so they should not rejoice in the goods of this world that they accumulate.

And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and We have raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service. And the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate﴾ [43].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 159:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them﴾ – the verse. We have already mentioned in surah al-Fatihah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor﴾ [al-Fatihah: 7], that the masculine plural forms and what resembles them, which are specific to a group of rational males, when they occur in the Book of Allah, exalted is He, or in the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ, the scholars have disagreed about whether women are included or not, unless there is evidence for their inclusion. By this you know that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and ask forgiveness for them﴾ may include women and may exclude them, based on the disagreement mentioned. However, He, exalted is He, has made clear in another place that they are included in a portion of His command to His Prophet ﷺ to seek forgiveness for them, and that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾ [Muhammad: 19].

The Almighty's statement: ﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has returned with anger from Allah?﴾ etc. In this verse He mentions that one who follows the pleasure of Allah is not like one who has returned with His anger, because the interrogative hamzah (*hamzat al-inkar*, the hamzah of rebuke) carries the meaning of negation (*nafy*). He does not mention here the attributes of one who follows the pleasure of Allah, but He points to some of them in another place, where He says: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it increased them in faith and they said, "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."﴾ ﴿So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty, no harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾ (p-216) [Ali 'Imran: 173–174].

And He points to some of the attributes of one who has returned with anger from Allah in His statement: ﴿You see many of them allying with those who disbelieve. Wretched is what their souls have put forth for them, that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide forever.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 80], and in His statement here: ﴿And whoever defrauds will come forth with what he defrauded﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 161].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 165:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Why, when a disaster struck you, although you had struck (the enemy) with twice as much, did you say, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ In this noble verse He mentions that what befell the Muslims on the Day of Uhud came to them only from their own selves. He did not explain the details of that here, but He detailed it in another place, which is His saying: ﴿And Allah had already fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 152]. This is the apparent meaning of the verse, because the best way to explain the Qur'an is by the Qur'an.

As for the other view, there is no explanation in the verse. The meaning of ﴿It is from yourselves﴾ according to it is that on the Day of Badr they were given the choice between killing the captives of Badr, or taking them captive and accepting ransom on condition that an equal number of them would be martyred in the following year. So they chose the ransom, on condition that seventy men equal to the captives of Badr would be martyred among them the following year, as related by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Ahmad al-Badawi al-Shinqiti included this in his poetic composition on the military campaigns (al-Maghazi) with his saying, in rajaz meter:

"The Muslims were given the choice between ransom, and that a number of them would be martyred in the next year,
And between killing them; so they inclined to ransom, because it strengthened them for fighting,
And because it led to martyrdom, which is the utmost of success and happiness."

His composition on the campaigns relies chiefly on "'Uyun al-Athar" by Ibn Sayyid al-Nas al-Ya'muri, who said in its introduction, in rajaz meter:

"A poem based on 'Uyun al-Athar, whose composition relies chiefly on the biographies (al-Siyar)."

Its commentator mentioned that the alif in his saying "yastashhidA" is substituted for the light emphatic nun (nun al-tawkid al-khafifah), and that it is in the verse like his saying, in madid meter: "Perhaps I fulfilled in a sign, that the northern winds lift my garment."

(p-217) According to this view, the meaning is: "Say, it is from yourselves," inasmuch as you chose the ransom and the martyrdom of a number equal to the captives from among yourselves.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 169:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ — the verse. In this verse, Allah, blessed and exalted, forbade the assumption that the martyrs are dead, and He declared that they are ﴿alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾, and that they are rejoicing ﴿in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, and ﴿rejoicing in those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾. Here He did not make clear whether this life of theirs in the barzakh is perceived by the people of this world or not. However, He made it clear in Surah "al-Baqarah" that they are not perceived, by His saying: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive﴾ [al-Baqarah: 154]; because the negation of perception indicates the negation of awareness a fortiori, as is evident.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 173:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you"﴾ — the verse.

A group of scholars said: the ones meant by "the people" who said, ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you﴾, were Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i, or a Bedouin from Khuza'ah, as Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Rafi'.

What supports this is the singular form of the one referred to in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is only that Satan frightens you of his allies﴾ — the verse [Al 'Imran: 175].

The author of al-Itqan said: al-Farisi said: Among what strengthens the view that the intended one is a single person is His saying: ﴿It is only that Satan﴾, where the demonstrative "that" (dhalikum) refers to one specific individual. Had the meaning been plural, He would have said: "It is only those (ulaika-kum) Satan." This is a clear indication in the wording. End of quotation from his words.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 178:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin; and for them is a humiliating punishment﴾. In this noble verse He mentions that He gives the disbelievers respite and allows them time so that their sin increases and their punishment is intensified. In another place He makes clear that He does not grant them this respite in ease except after He tests them with misfortune and adversity (al-ba'sa' wa'l-darra'). If they do not humble themselves, He pours upon them blessings and gives them more time until He seizes them suddenly, as in His saying: ﴿And We never sent a prophet to a town without seizing its people with adversity and hardship, that they might humble themselves﴾ ﴿Then We replaced the bad with good until they multiplied, and said: "Adversity and ease touched our fathers," so We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive﴾ [al-A'raf: 94], and His saying: ﴿And We had already sent [messengers] to nations before you, and We seized them with adversity and hardship that they might humble themselves﴾ ﴿So why, when Our might came to them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair﴾ [al-An'am: 44].

And He makes clear in another place that this gradual leading-on (istidraj) is from His mighty plan, as in His saying: ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know﴾ ﴿And I give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾ [al-Dukhan: 44-45 / 68].

And He makes clear in another place that the disbelievers are deceived by this istidraj, so they think it is a hastening of good things for them, and that on the Day of Resurrection they will be given better than what they were given in this world,

• as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children is [a sign that] We hasten to them in good things? Nay, they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55-56],

• and His saying: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ [Maryam: 77],

• and His saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36],

• and His saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat: 50],

• and His saying: ﴿And they said, "We are more in wealth and children..."﴾ the verse [Saba': 35].

As has already been mentioned. Al-ba'sa' means poverty and destitution, and al-darra' means illness according to the majority of scholars. Both are feminine verbal nouns (masdar) in form, with the feminine extended alif (alif al-ta'nith al-mamduda).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 186:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will surely be tested in your wealth and your persons, and you will surely hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah. But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, indeed that is of the matters requiring firm resolve.﴾ In this noble verse, He mentions that the believers will be tested in their wealth and their persons, and that they will hear much hurt from the People of the Book and the polytheists. And that if they are patient through that trial and harm and keep their duty to Allah, then their patience and piety are ﴿of the matters requiring firm resolve﴾, meaning: of the matters upon which firm resolve and determination should be held, because of their obligation.

He also explained in another place that among this trial is fear and hunger, and that the trial in persons and wealth is loss in them. He clarified in that place the outcome of the patience referred to here by His saying: ﴿that is of the matters requiring firm resolve﴾. That place is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will certainly test you with something of fear and hunger, and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits. But give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and they are the rightly guided.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 155–157], and by His saying: ﴿No disaster strikes except by the permission of Allah. And whoever believes in Allah – He guides his heart.﴾ [al-Taghabun: 11]. Included in His saying ﴿whoever believes in Allah﴾ is patience at the first shock; indeed some scholars restricted its meaning to that specifically, and what indicates its inclusion is His saying before it: ﴿No disaster strikes except by the permission of Allah﴾.

He also explained in another place that the quality of patience is not granted except to one who possesses a great share and a great fortune, and that is His saying: ﴿But none receives it except those who are patient, and none receives it except one of great fortune.﴾ [Fussilat: 35]. And He explained in another place that the reward of patience has no reckoning, and that is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account.﴾ [az-Zumar: 10].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 3, verse 191:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾ In this verse He mentions that among what the people of understanding (ulu al-albab) say is the declaration of their Lord's transcendence above having created the heavens and the earth in vain, without wisdom. Exalted is He, the Most High, far above that with great exaltation.

In another place He explicitly states that those who suppose this are the disbelievers, and He threatens them for that evil supposition with woe from the Fire, in His saying: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.﴾ [Sad: 27].

The words of Allah, ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾, do not specify here what He has prepared for the righteous. However, He clarified it in another place, that it is delight (al-na'im), as in His words: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in delight﴾ [al-Infitar: 13]. And He clarified in another place that among that delight is drinking from a cup whose mixture is camphor, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor﴾ [al-Insan: 5].
